title: How far the 4,571-gene functional-annotation map is from a parameter set a whole-organism developmental simulation could run on
constraint: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) is the proxy. No flying-fish molecular data exists. No bird data was used or fetched: Aves is this project's frozen holdout.

BRENDA.finding: The open BRENDA endpoint exposes enzymes, reactions, inhibitors, activators, cofactors, tissues and references, and NO kinetic value at all: there is no Km, kcat, Ki or Kd class or predicate in the whole graph. Bulk kinetic data is behind a licence form. The website search for 'Danio rerio' returned 'Sorry, no results could be found for your query!'

f.note_on_count: counted as distinct secreted molecules with a fetched diffusion coefficient, not as genes; the assumed Shh placeholder is excluded

repo_own_fetch.stage_caveat: Every measured value below comes from the zebrafish GASTRULA, because that is where FCS and FRAP on morphogens have been done. The first validation target is a PECTORAL FIN BUD at 72 hpf. Carrying a gastrula diffusion coefficient to a fin bud is an assumption, not a measurement, and every result that depends on it inherits that.

f.verdict: Diffusion coefficients exist for 4 secreted zebrafish molecules (Fgf8a, Lefty2, Squint, Cyclops), all measured in the GASTRULA, 2 read in a primary source and the rest quoted second-hand. Shh in the fin bud, which is what the first validation target needs, is an explicit placeholder. Of the 4,571 genes, 4 have this parameter.

whole_zebrafish_proteome.reading: For the WHOLE zebrafish proteome, STRING v12 has about 3,873 edges with direct experimental evidence, touching 612 proteins, against about 4,070,667 edges whose experimental evidence is orthology-transferred from another species. The zebrafish interactome is overwhelmingly inferred.

STRING_v12_zebrafish.caveat: STRING edges are UNDIRECTED and UNSIGNED and carry a confidence score, not a strength. The 'experiments' channel is physical/biochemical interaction evidence, not regulation. None of this is a signed directed regulatory edge.

bionumbers.finding: BioNumbers holds 19 zebrafish entries in total. Every one is organismal or cell-biophysical: embryo length, egg diameter, mass, genome size, GC content, cell-cycle length, neuron and cell counts, energy density, cell migration speeds, a cortical friction coefficient, and one protein RELOCALISATION half-time (myosin II to the cortex, ~20 s, which is not a degradation half-life). Not one is a per-gene rate constant: no mRNA or protein half-life, no transcription rate, no Km, Kd or Hill coefficient, no morphogen diffusion coefficient.

europe_pmc_literature_hits.note: Paper counts, NOT parameter counts. Recorded only to show whether the measurement exists for zebrafish anywhere in the literature. A hit count of several hundred with zero database rows means the numbers are locked in figures and prose, not in a table a simulation could read.

what_we_actually_hold.note: The real parameter set, sized honestly. These are good numbers; they are just not a per-gene dynamical parameter set.

functional_annotation.caveat: Pathway membership is NOT causation and not a claim about the fin. A gene appears here because a database places it in a process or map, often computationally: GO IEA and Reactome IEA rows are electronic annotations, and every Reactome zebrafish entry is inferred by orthology from human. Membership does not show that the gene acts in that pathway in the pectoral fin, at any stage, or in a flying fish. Graded causal evidence is in genotype/causal-chains.json.

worked_example.why: One species states the annotation-versus-parameter gap better than any aggregate: a genome with essentially complete functional annotation and, in the paper that reports it, none of the eight parameters.

paper.title: Draft Genome of the Mirrorwing Flyingfish (Hirundichthys speculiger).
paper.authors: Xu P, Zhao C, You X, Yang F, Chen J, Ruan Z, Gu R, Xu J, Bian C, Shi Q.
paper.read: full text and both supplementary archives, fetched and parsed by this script

annotation.quote_abstract: The assembled genome was predicted to possess 23,611 protein-coding genes, of which 23,492 (99.5%) were functionally annotated with public databases. A total of 42.02% genome sequences consisted of repeat element
annotation.quote_results: We predicted 23,611 protein-coding genes in the mirrorwing flyingfish genome, with an average gene length of 14.35 kb. Moreover, 99.50% of these genes could be functionally annotated by at least one of the four popular databases, with 20,692 KEGG hits, 21,453 SwissProt hits, 23,477 TrEMBL hits, and 21,888 Interpro hits
annotation.definition_caveat: 'Functionally annotated' here means at least one hit in at least one of four databases. TrEMBL alone supplies 23,477 of the 23,492, and a TrEMBL hit is a sequence-similarity match to an unreviewed entry, not a measured function. Annotation by homology is the weakest sense of the word.

parameters_in_the_paper.method: every term below counted in the fetched full-text XML (all sections present: Materials and Methods through References) and in Data_Sheet_2.docx, which holds the supplementary tables
parameters_in_the_paper.gene_prediction_evidence: homology plus ab initio (Augustus); the word transcriptome does not appear, and 'expression' appears twice, both times in discussion of other work or in a reference title
parameters_in_the_paper.verdict: Zero. No RNA-seq, no absolute or relative expression, no protein or mRNA half-life, no binding affinity, no kinetics, no diffusion coefficient, no Hill coefficient and no gene regulatory network appear anywhere in the paper or its supplement. Supplementary Data Sheet 1 is twelve TIFF figures; Data Sheet 2 holds 14 supplementary tables, all of them accessions, assembly statistics and gene-family counts.

worked_example.the_point: 99.5%% of 23,611 genes functionally annotated, 0 of 8 simulation parameters. Functional annotation and parameterisation are not the same quantity, and in the one species this project is about, the first is nearly complete while the second is empty.

ratio.definition: Minimal parameter count = 4 per gene (items a-d: absolute abundance, protein half-life, mRNA half-life, transcription rate) + 1 strength per edge of the edge list we could actually assemble.

lenient_variant.what_is_relaxed: item (a) satisfied by a PaxDb ppm value in any whole-organism or organ dataset, ignoring the cell type, the stage and the unit

extended_variant.what_is_added: items e, f, g as well: kinetics, diffusion, cooperativity, one each per gene, so 7 per gene plus one per edge

precedent_m_genitalium.why: The closest thing that exists to what is being asked: a model that predicts phenotype from genotype for every annotated gene of an organism.

paper.title: A whole-cell computational model predicts phenotype from genotype.
paper.authors: Karr JR, Sanghvi JC, Macklin DN, Gutschow MV, Jacobs JM, Bolival B, Assad-Garcia N, Glass JI, Covert MW.
paper.note: The Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returned 500 for this PMCID; the text was read from the NCBI PMC efetch XML instead.

what_it_covered.genes_quote: Mycoplasma genitalium, a human urogenital parasite whose genome contains 525 genes ( Fraser et al
what_it_covered.sub_models_quote: We divided M. genitalium into the 28 functional processes illustrated in Figure 1 , and modeled each process independently on a 1 s time scale using different mathematics and different experimental data.
what_it_covered.scope: the life cycle of a SINGLE CELL; no anatomy, no tissues, no development

what_it_took.quote: Our model is based on a synthesis of over 900 publications and includes more than 1,900 experimentally observed parameters.
what_it_took.reconstruction_quote: The whole-cell model was based on a detailed reconstruction of M. genitalium developed from over 900 primary sources, reviews, books, and databases.

scaled_to_our_gene_set.note: Not a prediction, just the same parameter density applied to a larger gene set, to size the task. Development would need more, not fewer, parameters per gene: a zygote-to-adult model adds cell states, positions, divisions and movements that a single bacterial cell does not have.

precedent_m_genitalium.the_difference: M. genitalium is one cell with 525 genes, and it still took over 900 publications and more than 1,900 measured parameters. The question here is a whole organism from the zygote, with 4,571 genes and a body plan. The precedent does not say the task is impossible; it says the unit of work is a parameter read from a paper, roughly 3.6 per gene, and that functional annotation was the starting point of that effort, not a substitute for it: the paper's own claim is that the model 'accounts for all annotated gene functions', which it reached by curating 900 sources on top of the annotation.

headline.one_sentence: Of the 18,733 numbers a minimal dynamical model of these 4,571 genes would need, we hold 0, because the eight parameter classes a simulation runs on are not what any of the queried databases stores for zebrafish.
headline.generous_caveat: and all 2972 of those are PaxDb ppm values, a share of total protein mass in a whole organism or a dissected organ, not a count per cell in a named cell type at a named stage
headline.annotation_for_contrast: 3857 of 4571 genes (84.4%) carry a functional annotation

yes.what: A reaction-diffusion model of one morphogen gradient over a continuum, not over genes
yes.with: the 4 fetched zebrafish diffusion coefficients plus the Fgf8 residence time and gradient length in sim-engine/params/zebrafish-morphogens.json
yes.coarseness: concentration in arbitrary units, one tissue, gastrula parameters carried to whatever stage is being modelled, which the file itself flags as an assumption

yes.what: A 2-node Boolean or qualitative model of the fin-size switch
yes.with: the 5 signed directed gene-gene edges in genotype/causal-chains.json cross_gene (kcnh2a, lat4a, kcnk5b, calcineurin) and the 12 calibrated interventions
yes.coarseness: signs and orderings, no rates; outcomes as larger / smaller / unchanged

yes.what: A growth and allometry trajectory for the whole animal
yes.with: development/ (staging, growth, allometry) and physiology/ (25 fetched sources)
yes.coarseness: whole-organism, no genes in the loop; the genotype enters only through the 12 calibrated knobs on 19 morphology parameters

yes.what: A curated small network over a handful of cell states: the project's own estimate of its ceiling
yes.with: the 42 causal chains, the 30 tissue-to-tissue and cell-to-cell interactions, and the 449 experimentally supported STRING edges as a candidate topology
yes.coarseness: topology and sign where known; every rate constant would be a free parameter fitted or assumed, so the model would be a hypothesis generator, not a prediction

no: A zygote-to-adult simulation in which the 4,571 genes are dynamical variables.
Any model whose output depends on absolute concentrations, since not one gene has one, and ppm cannot be converted without a total protein count per zebrafish cell that no fetched source gives.
Any model whose output depends on timescales, since no gene has an mRNA or protein half-life and no gene has a transcription rate: every timescale would be invented.

A genome-scale regulatory network: 0.004% of gene pairs have direct experimental support, none of it signed, directed and quantified. The only genome-scale option is orthology transfer from human CollecTRI (17,804 transferable edges), which is a hypothesis list, not zebrafish data.
Anything at all in a flying fish: see the worked example.
what_would_change_the_answer: A staged zebrafish absolute-proteomics dataset in copies per cell (none exists in PaxDb or PRIDE).
A genome-wide zebrafish mRNA stability dataset turned into a per-gene table.
A zebrafish TF-target resource with signs, so the network stops being orthology transfer.
